answer: Arrival-Jitter Admission Gate. Each identity must submit its first ten actions with inter-arrival gaps drawn from a heavy-tailed human distribution; a sparrow-like steady drip or machine-precise cadence is rejected. The gate scores burstiness and requires a slow, irregular warm-up before full throughput, with a small opal deposit held per identity during probation. Attackers must either fake realistic timing across thousands of accounts, raising compute and orchestration cost per identity, or accept throttled ember-slow ramp-up that makes mass registration economically pointless.
